item.title: Trans. Visible. Unapologetic.
item.description: How can my mold-breaking trans body fit into such narrow understandings of what professionalism can look like, and with that, what a doctor can look like?

item.title: What my asexuality and imposter syndrome are teaching me about belonging

item.title: Gatekeeping in STEM is a symptom of epistemicide
item.description: Epistemicide is “the killing, silencing, annihilation, or devaluing” of epistemologies, or systems of knowledge.

item.title: We need more STEM Black Girl Magic on our screens, and we won’t wait around for it
item.description: As a young Black girl growing up, I remember not seeing many scientists who looked like me.

item.title: Dreams Built on Myths: Of Science and the American Dream
item.description: As a Latinx, woman of color, immigrant scientist trained in the United States, science was at the heart of my American Dream.

item.title: International STEM students need funding opportunities, too — especially now
item.description: It is virtually impossible for international students to seek financial stability, and the pandemic has compounded the difficulties faced by international students.

item.title: A life of the neurodivergent mind
item.description: I entered graduate school thinking I’d live a “life of the mind.” I just didn’t think it’d be my mind specifically.

item.title: Community College, Beyond the Bias
item.description: My path was hardly the “traditional” college student’s story.

item.title: Having ADHD doesn’t mean you’re not cut out for STEM
item.description: Too often, educators mistake the symptoms of ADHD for a lack of care or interest in the subject.

item.title: Dr. Sandra Steingraber: “I did not become a biologist to write eulogies for the species I study”
item.description: As extinction rates accelerate, scientists get louder. Dr. Sandra Steingraber spoke these words at the Citigroup headquarters before being arrested in protest of the financing of fossil fuels.
